outcome: additional treatment need (epidural blood patch, caffeine, paracetamol)
cohort: 180 obstetric subjects with ASA II/III status, aged 18-35 years, experiencing post-dural puncture headache (PDPH) following cesarean section under spinal anesthesia.
finding: Nebulization with dexmedetomidine significantly decreased pain scores and the need for additional analgesic therapy in subjects with PDPH compared to nebulized fentanyl and saline.
mod_finding: All participants in the study had undergone a cesarean section; the mode of birth itself was not a variable investigated for its effect on outcomes.
